name: Karakeep (bookmarks, tags, smart lists, stats)
param_style: drizzle-orm 0.45 query builder on better-sqlite3; ? positional, IN lists expanded per call; relational queries emit json_group_array subqueries
schema_source: all drizzle migrations (packages/db/drizzle/*.sql) applied to an empty database, then .schema of the tables the queries touch (indexes are the app's own; packages/db/schema.ts is the source of truth)
data_scale: scale 1: 5 users, 40k bookmarks (u1 owns 36k; 80 % links / 12 % texts / 8 % assets) over six years skewed recent, 32k bookmarkLinks over a Zipf-like set of ~420 domains, 5.8k tags (u1: 3.5k used + 300 unused), 296k tagsOnBookmarks with Zipf-like tag popularity (top tag on 8 % of bookmarks, 75 % attachedBy ai), 82 lists (u1: 30 manual + 40 smart), 17k list memberships, 56k assets, 7k highlights; ~55 MB. Mirrors #3088's 42k bookmarks / 348k tag links / 40 smart lists.

cpu_evidence.summary: lists.stats took 16.3 s warm on a Raspberry Pi (42k bookmarks, 348k tag links, 40 smart lists, SQLite 3.46.1): the tagName matcher's correlated EXISTS ran per bookmark; tag-first join order (PR #3089) cut it to 2.3 s, and the pinned code now uses an IN subquery
web UI took ~30 s to show bookmarks after an update; reporter later saw 2-4 s queries and 'database is locked' with a 25 MB DB on a NAS bind mount (I/O as much as CPU)

visibility_note: 30k stars, popular self-hosted read-later app (formerly Hoarder); SQLite is the only supported database
interest_note: Smart lists compile a search query language into nested IN / EXISTS / NOT EXISTS / LIKE conditions; lists.stats runs one count per smart list. getBookmarks is a CTE top-N then a 6-way LEFT JOIN fan-out; tag and stats pages are big GROUP BYs, including a CASE/INSTR/SUBSTR domain extraction.
